title: What Happens When Your AI Agent Is Wrong?
author: Srilakshmi Chiluvuri
source: Leadership in Change (Substack, guest post), August 6, 2026
summary: This guest post on Leadership in Change, written by Srilakshmi Chiluvuri, tackles why companies keep paying AI agent developers even when free open-source agents are available on GitHub: those agents can execute tasks but cannot judge context, priority, or risk, and the piece opens with a real incident where a single misrouted escalation cost one company three enterprise customers within 48 hours. The failure, Chiluvuri argues, is almost always architectural — the fix required agent memory, guardrails, multi-agent routing, and human escalation when the system's confidence drops. She offers ALIGN as a five-step leadership checklist for deploying agents responsibly: Assess repetitive work, Locate decision bottlenecks, Integrate context sources, Govern with guardrails, and measure business outcomes. The piece closes by framing AI-agent success as an organizational-design and governance challenge for leaders.
points: Explains why companies still pay for AI agent development even though open-source agents are free: raw agents can act but can't judge context, priority, or risk.
Anchors the argument in a real incident — a misrouted escalation that cost one company three enterprise customers in 48 hours.
Introduces the ALIGN framework (Assess, Locate, Integrate, Govern, measure outcomes) as a practical deployment checklist for leaders.
Reframes the leadership question from 'how many agents should we deploy' to 'what happens when this agent is wrong.'
Positions responsible AI-agent deployment as an organizational-design and governance problem, not just a technical one.
quotes: Free agents can execute tasks, but they can't weigh context, priority, or risk. That gap is the whole problem.
The failure is almost always architecture, not the agent itself.
A single misrouted escalation cost one company three enterprise customers in 48 hours.
Four things fixed it: agent memory, guardrails, multi-agent routing, and human escalation when confidence drops.
ALIGN is her deployment checklist: Assess repetitive work, Locate bottlenecks, Integrate context, Govern with guardrails, and measure outcomes.
Before you deploy any agent, answer five questions. Start with the one most of us skip: what happens when the agent is wrong?
Identify tasks that consume significant time but require limited creativity, judgment, or strategic thinking.
